samples.label: tools/list

tools.name: list_skills
tools.title: List Skills
tools.description: List the available skills (tool groups) — project, documents, search, analysis, compilation, credentials, memory, relationships, advanced — with a description, the tool count, whether the skill is already active, and its tool names. Use this to discover capabilities, then call use_skill to activate a group whose tools you need. Takes no parameters.

name.description: Skill identifier passed to use_skill.

tools.description: Number of visible tools in the skill.

activated.description: Whether the skill is already active this session.

tool_names.description: Names of the visible tools in the skill.

tools.name: use_skill
tools.title: Activate Skill
tools.description: Activate a skill so its tools become available to call. Returns the activated skill's tool names and their schemas; clients that support tools/list_changed will also see the new tools appear automatically. Call list_skills first to see the available skill names. Tools activate when requested; already active skills return the same complete schemas.

name.description: The skill to activate, e.g. "documents", "search", or "analysis". Get valid names from list_skills.

tools.name: read_result
tools.title: Read Large Result
tools.description: Retrieve a bounded UTF-8 chunk of a large compiled or analysis result using its opaque resultId. Continue using nextOffset until null, then concatenate text in order to reconstruct the original JSON. Available without filesystem tools. Results expire after one hour, on server restart, or when the 64 MiB/256-result cache fills.

resultId.description: Opaque _ref or resultId returned by the original operation.

offset.description: UTF-8 byte offset, initially zero; subsequent calls use nextOffset.

limit.description: Maximum UTF-8 bytes of chunk text, default 16384; characters are never split. MCP serialization overhead is additional.

text.description: This UTF-8 chunk of the original compact JSON.

nextOffset.description: Next byte offset, or null after the final chunk.

totalBytes.description: Byte length of the complete result.

tools.name: open_project
tools.title: Open Scrivener Project
tools.description: Open a Scrivener project and make it the active project for this session. Every document, structure, search, and analysis tool operates on the project opened here, so call this first. Accepts the path to a .scriv folder or the .scrivx file inside it and resolves the project automatically. Returns the project title, author, and metadata. Opening a project closes any project already open. If you do not know the path, call discover_projects first.

path.description: Path to the Scrivener project: either the .scriv folder (e.g. "~/Documents/My Novel.scriv") or the .scrivx file inside it. Absolute or ~-relative.

readOnly.description: Open the project for authoritative reads only; mutation tools reject even when force is set.

tools.name: get_structure
tools.title: Get Project Structure
tools.description: Return the binder hierarchy of the open project: its folders and documents in tree order, each with id, title, type, depth, and word count. Use this to understand the manuscript layout and to obtain the document ids that read_document, write_document, and the analysis tools require. By default returns a compact flat array of [id, title, type, depth, wordCount, hasChildren] tuples to save tokens; set summaryOnly for just project-level counts. Requires an open project (call open_project first).

maxDepth.description: Maximum depth to descend into the binder tree, starting at 0 for top-level items. Omit to return the full hierarchy.

folderId.description: UUID of a binder folder, as returned by get_structure.

includeTrash.description: Set true to include trashed items in the result. Default false.

summaryOnly.description: When true, skip the tree and return only project-level counts (documents, words) plus title and author. Default false.

flat.description: When true (default), return a compact flat array of [id, title, type, depth, wordCount, hasChildren] tuples. When false, return the nested tree object.

documents.description: Flat list of binder items in tree order (present unless summaryOnly).

id.description: Document/folder UUID for read_document etc.

title.description: Item title as shown in the binder.

wordCount.description: Word count of the item (0 for folders).

hasChildren.description: Whether the item contains nested items.

summary.description: Project-level counts plus title and author (present when summaryOnly).

structure.description: Nested binder tree (present when flat is false).

tools.name: refresh_project
tools.title: Reload Project From Disk
tools.description: Reload the open project from disk, discarding the in-memory cache. Use this when the project has been changed by the Scrivener app or another process while open here, so that subsequent reads reflect the latest saved state. Requires an open project. Takes no parameters.

tools.name: close_project
tools.title: Close Project
tools.description: Close the currently open project, flush any pending memory/auto-save state, and clear the active session. After this, document and analysis tools have no project to act on until open_project is called again. Use this to switch projects cleanly or release file handles at the end of a session. Requires an open project. Takes no parameters.

tools.name: discover_projects
tools.title: Discover Scrivener Projects
tools.description: Scan common locations (Documents, Desktop, and iCloud Mobile Documents) for Scrivener projects and return the paths of every .scriv folder found, searching up to three levels deep. Use this when the user refers to their project by name rather than path ("open my novel"): present the results and pass the chosen path to open_project. Does not open anything itself. Returns a list of project paths, or a message if none are found.

searchPath.description: Optional extra directory to search in addition to the default locations, e.g. an external drive or a custom projects folder. Absolute or ~-relative path.

projects.description: Absolute paths of the .scriv projects found.

tools.name: detect_open_project
tools.title: Detect Open Scrivener Project
tools.description: Detect which Scrivener project the user currently has open in the desktop Scrivener app, so you can act on it without asking for a path. Use this when the user says "my project", "the project I have open", or gives a command with no project specified. Reads the open window names from the running app and resolves them to .scriv paths on disk; it does not open anything. If exactly one project is open, pass its path to open_project. macOS only right now (returns supported=false elsewhere; fall back to discover_projects). The first use may prompt macOS to allow the client app to control Scrivener.

searchPath.description: Optional extra directory to resolve project names against, in addition to the default locations. Absolute or ~-relative path.

supported.description: False on platforms where detection is not implemented (non-macOS).

running.description: Whether the Scrivener app appears to be running.

openProjects.description: Open projects resolved to a .scriv path.

name.description: Project name as shown in the Scrivener window title.

path.description: Absolute path to the matching .scriv folder.

unresolved.description: Open project names that could not be matched to a .scriv folder on disk.

tools.name: get_compile_settings
tools.title: Get Compile & Taxonomy Settings
tools.description: Return the project's compile-format definitions (from Settings/compile.xml) and its taxonomy: the named compile formats and their section-layout counts, the current output file type, label and status definitions (with colors), saved collections, and user-defined section types. Use this to discover what compile formats and metadata categories a project defines before compiling or organizing. Read-only; does not run a compile. If a project has never been compiled, hasCompileSettings is false and only the taxonomy is returned. Requires an open project (call open_project first).

hasCompileSettings.description: False when Settings/compile.xml is absent or unreadable.

currentFileType.description: Default output file type of the last-used compile (e.g. "pdf").

compileFormats.description: Named compile formats the project defines.

id.description: Format identifier.

sectionLayoutCount.description: Number of section-type to layout assignments.

hasFrontMatter.description: Whether the format injects default front/back matter.

sectionTypes.description: User-defined section types (Scene, Chapter, Part Heading, ...).

id.description: Section-type UUID.

name.description: Human-readable name.

id.description: Label id.
Status id.
Collection UUID.

tools.name: get_manuscript_briefing
tools.title: Manuscript Briefing
tools.description: One "where am I?" snapshot of the whole manuscript: total word count against the project draft target (with percent-to-goal and deadline), document/folder counts, the per-status and per-label breakdown, and the longest and shortest documents. Use this right after open_project to orient before diving in, instead of stitching get_statistics, get_writing_goals, and get_compile_settings together. Read-only. Requires an open project.

words.description: Word-count progress against the draft target.

draftTarget.description: Project draft word target, if set in Scrivener.

percentToTarget.description: total / draftTarget as a percentage, if a target is set.

byStatus.description: Count of text documents per status (e.g. To Do, Done).

byLabel.description: Count of text documents per label.

longest.description: Longest text document by word count, or null.

id.description: Document UUID.

shortest.description: Shortest text document by word count, or null.

id.description: Document UUID.

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.title: List Document Snapshots
tools.description: List the snapshots Scrivener has saved of a project's documents (from the .scriv package's Snapshots/ directory). Pass documentId to list one document's snapshots, or omit it to list snapshots for every document that has any. Each entry gives the owning document id and title, a snapshotId (pass it to read_snapshot to get the text), the snapshot's title, and its date. Read-only. Returns an empty list when nothing has been snapshotted. Requires an open project (call open_project first).

documentId.description: UUID of a single document to list snapshots for. Omit to list all documents.

documents.description: One entry per document that has snapshots.

documentId.description: Document UUID.

documentTitle.description: Document title, if the document is still in the binder.

tools.name: read_snapshot
tools.title: Read Document Snapshot
tools.description: Return the text of a single document snapshot. Pass the documentId and the snapshotId from list_snapshots. The snapshot's RTF is converted to plain text. Read-only; does not alter the document or restore the snapshot. Requires an open project (call open_project first).

documentId.description: UUID of the document.
UUID of the document.

snapshotId.description: Id of the snapshot that was read.

wordCount.description: Word count of the snapshot text.

tools.name: compare_snapshot
tools.title: Compare Snapshot
tools.description: Compare a document snapshot against the current document text, or against another snapshot (pass againstSnapshotId). Returns the paragraphs added and removed and the net word-count change — use this to see what changed since a snapshot was taken. Read-only. Requires an open project (call open_project first). Get snapshot ids from list_snapshots.

documentId.description: UUID of the document.

againstSnapshotId.description: Optional second snapshot id to compare against. Omit to compare against the current document text.

documentId.description: UUID of the compared document.

to.description: What it was compared against ("current" or a snapshot id).

wordDelta.description: to.wordCount minus from.wordCount (negative means text was cut).

wordsAdded.description: Words present in the compared-to text but not the snapshot (word-level).

wordsRemoved.description: Words present in the snapshot but not the compared-to text (word-level).

addedParagraphs.description: Paragraphs present in the compared-to text but not the snapshot.

removedParagraphs.description: Paragraphs present in the snapshot but not the compared-to text.

unchangedParagraphs.description: Count of paragraphs common to both.

tools.name: create_snapshot
tools.title: Create Document Snapshot
tools.description: Take a Scrivener-native snapshot of a document's current content, restorable from Scrivener's own Snapshots browser. Use this before rewriting a document to give the writer a native rollback point. Copies the live content into the project's Snapshots directory with a title and timestamp; does not modify the document. Requires an open project and a document that has content.

documentId.description: UUID of the document to snapshot.

title.description: Snapshot title shown in Scrivener. Defaults to "Snapshot".

documentId.description: UUID of the snapshotted document.

snapshotId.description: Id of the new snapshot (for read_snapshot).

tools.name: verify_project_integrity
tools.title: Verify Project Integrity
tools.description: Scan the open project for structural problems and return a read-only report: binder entries with missing, malformed, or duplicate UUIDs, entries missing their type, and text documents whose backing content is unreadable or empty. Use when a project looks corrupted, after manual edits to the .scrivx file, or before a bulk operation; not when you just want the document tree (use get_structure) or a single document (use get_document_info). This tool only detects problems and never repairs them. related: get_structure, get_document_info. Requires an open project.

includeTrash.description: Whether to also verify documents in the project trash. Defaults to true so the whole project is checked; set false to skip trashed items.

ok.description: True when no error-severity issues were found.

issues.description: Every integrity problem found; empty when the project is clean.

kind.description: Stable machine-readable problem category, e.g. "missing_id", "duplicate_id", "empty_content".

id.description: Scrivener UUID of the offending item, when known.

summary.description: One-line human-readable summary of the check.

tools.name: manuscript_dashboard
tools.title: Interactive Manuscript Dashboard
tools.description: Browse the binder, scene summaries, character appearances, measured pacing and unresolved continuity evidence; select a scene to read its saved manuscript context. MCP Apps clients receive an accessible interactive view, and all clients retain the same structured data and text. Review controls use review_changes.

reviewDocumentId.description: Limit the revision inbox to this scene.

documentId.description: Optional saved scene UUID to reveal.

limit.description: Number of manuscript scenes per page.

projectTitle.description: Human-readable title of the selected project.

projectId.description: Stable project identity shared with evidence and search.

uiSupported.description: Whether the connected client negotiated MCP Apps HTML support.

binder.description: Active binder hierarchy, including folder and document UUIDs and titles.

scenes.description: Manuscript scenes in binder order, with source revision, synopsis, word count, pacing measurements and character appearances.

documentId.description: Stable binder document UUID.

revision.description: SHA-256 of the saved RTF source.

pacing.description: Existing local pacing analysis; a heuristic, not a claim of narrative intent.

name.description: Character name or alias matched as text.

mentions.description: First 100 located name mentions in saved manuscript order.

start.description: Inclusive UTF-16 source offset.

end.description: Exclusive UTF-16 source offset.

quote.description: Matched name with up to 80 surrounding UTF-16 characters on either side.

truncated.description: True when additional name mentions exist beyond the first 100 returned passages; the returned length is not a complete occurrence count.

appearances.description: Name and alias text mentions with source offsets; mentions do not establish factual presence.

findings.description: Unresolved continuity findings with supporting revision-bound source passages.

inbox.description: Filtered revision summaries, edit decision totals and next-page cursor.

proposals.description: Persistent review proposals, edit states and application identities.

applications.description: Durable application history for revision-guarded undo after restarting the server.

context.description: Selected saved scene, up to 20000 UTF-16 characters, with exact document identity and revision; null until selected.

historyPagination.description: Independent bounded history cursors; null means complete.

proposals.description: Next proposal cursor, or null after the last proposal.

applications.description: Next application cursor, or null after the last application.

findings.description: Next unresolved finding cursor, or null after the last finding.

pagination.description: Offset, returned count and total manuscript scenes.

tools.name: get_document_info
tools.title: Get Document Info
tools.description: Return metadata for a single document without its body text: title, type, word count, synopsis, label, status, parent, and custom metadata. Use this to inspect a document or to read its word count cheaply; call read_document when you need the actual prose, or get_structure for the whole binder. Requires an open project and a valid document id.

documentId.description: Scrivener document UUID, as returned by get_structure (a binder item "id").

id.description: Scrivener UUID of the document.

wordCount.description: Word count of the document body.

includeInCompile.description: Whether the document is included in compile.

customMetadata.description: Map of custom metadata field names to string values.

path.description: Ancestor chain from the binder root to the document.

id.description: UUID of the ancestor binder item.

metadata.description: Derived metadata map (synopsis, notes, keywords, status, label) as strings.

tools.name: read_document
tools.title: Read Document
tools.description: Read the text of a single document. By default returns plain text; set format to "formatted" to get rich text with styling and structure preserved. Use offset and limit to page through long documents by word range instead of returning the whole thing. Use get_document_info when you only need metadata, or search/semantic_search to find content across many documents. Requires an open project and a valid document id.

documentId.description: Scrivener document UUID, as returned by get_structure (a binder item "id").

format.description: "plain" (default) returns unstyled text and supports offset/limit paging. "formatted" returns rich text with styling and structure preserved (paged reading does not apply).

offset.description: Zero-based word index to start reading from. Default 0. Plain format only.

limit.description: Maximum number of words to return from offset. Omit to read to the end.

tools.name: write_document
tools.title: Write Document
tools.description: Replace a document's text with new content, preserving the surrounding Scrivener formatting the edit did not touch (stylesheet, styles, images, footnotes) byte-for-byte. The result reports whether formatting was fully preserved; when an edit would drop non-round-trippable content it takes a Scrivener snapshot first (restorable in Scrivener) and says so. To change only the title or metadata use update_document; to add a new document use create_document. Requires an open project and a valid document id.

documentId.description: Scrivener document UUID, as returned by get_structure (a binder item "id").

content.description: Document body as plain text. May be empty.

force.description: Explicitly acknowledge native-app overwrite risk when Scrivener is open or detection is ambiguous. Default false. Never overrides saved revision checks or another server instance.

expectedRevision.description: SHA-256 saved source revision from read_document or manuscript_dashboard; stale writes are rejected.

allowFormattingLoss.description: Explicitly acknowledge disclosed formatting risk. Prefer review_changes preview before applying a lossy change.

tools.name: create_document
tools.title: Create Document
tools.description: Create a new text document or folder in the binder and return its new id. Optionally set the initial body content and the parent folder; if no parent is given the item is added at the top level. Each call creates a distinct item (not idempotent). Use write_document to change content afterward. Requires an open project.

title.description: Title for the new document or folder. Truncated to 255 characters.

content.description: Document body as plain text. May be empty.

parentId.description: UUID of a binder folder, as returned by get_structure.

documentType.description: Whether to create a "Text" document (default) or a "Folder".

force.description: Explicitly acknowledge native-app overwrite risk when Scrivener is open or detection is ambiguous. Default false. Never overrides saved revision checks or another server instance.

documentId.description: Scrivener UUID of the newly created document or folder.

tools.name: delete_document
tools.title: Delete Document
tools.description: Move a document to the project trash. This is reversible: the document can be listed with list_trash and brought back with restore_document until the trash is emptied in Scrivener. Deleting an already-trashed document is a no-op. Requires an open project and a valid document id.

documentId.description: Scrivener document UUID, as returned by get_structure (a binder item "id").

force.description: Explicitly acknowledge native-app overwrite risk when Scrivener is open or detection is ambiguous. Default false. Never overrides saved revision checks or another server instance.

dryRun.description: Validate and preview the structural change without writing. Reuse the returned expectedRevision when applying.

expectedRevision.description: Binder revision returned by a structural preview. A changed binder rejects the operation.

tools.name: move_document
tools.title: Move Document
tools.description: Move a document or folder to a different parent folder in the binder, optionally at a specific position among the target folder's children. Changes only the location, not the content. Requires an open project, a valid document id, and a valid target folder id.

documentId.description: Scrivener document UUID, as returned by get_structure (a binder item "id").

targetFolderId.description: UUID of a binder folder, as returned by get_structure.

force.description: Explicitly acknowledge native-app overwrite risk when Scrivener is open or detection is ambiguous. Default false. Never overrides saved revision checks or another server instance.

dryRun.description: Validate and preview the structural change without writing. Reuse the returned expectedRevision when applying.

expectedRevision.description: Binder revision returned by a structural preview. A changed binder rejects the operation.

position.description: Zero-based index at which to insert the item among the target folder's children. Omit to append at the end.

tools.name: update_document
tools.title: Update Document Title & Metadata
tools.description: Update a document's title and/or its metadata (synopsis, notes, label, status, and custom fields) in a single call. Pass only the fields you want to change; omitted fields are left untouched. To change the body text use write_document; to move it use move_document. Requires an open project and a valid document id.

documentId.description: Scrivener document UUID, as returned by get_structure (a binder item "id").

force.description: Explicitly acknowledge native-app overwrite risk when Scrivener is open or detection is ambiguous. Default false. Never overrides saved revision checks or another server instance.

title.description: New title for the document. Omit to leave the title unchanged.

synopsis.description: Synopsis / index-card text shown in the Scrivener outliner.

label.description: Label name. A new name creates a gray label; an empty string clears the assignment.

status.description: Status name (e.g. "First Draft"). A new name creates a status; an empty string clears it.

customMetadata.description: Map of custom metadata field names to string values.

tools.name: review_changes
tools.title: Review Proposed Manuscript Changes
tools.description: Persist revision-bound edits, preview before/after without changing the manuscript, apply selected edits or batches with native snapshots, reject edits, recover interrupted applications, and undo only when the saved document still matches the applied revision. Formatting loss requires explicit acknowledgment.

action.description: Review operation. Propose and preview never modify the manuscript.

limit.description: History page size, default20; list returns proposal summaries. Use get for full proposal details.

documentId.description: Source document UUID for a proposal.

proposalId.description: Persistent proposal UUID for preview, reject or apply.

proposalIds.description: Proposal UUIDs for a recoverable batch application (up to 100).

editIds.description: Selected proposal edit UUIDs; omitted means all pending edits.

expectedRevision.description: SHA-256 saved document revision; stale proposals and writes are rejected.

edits.description: Non-overlapping replacements using UTF-16 offsets in the source text.

start.description: Inclusive source text offset.

end.description: Exclusive source text offset.

category.description: Issue category for a proposal or inbox filter.

rationale.description: Why this proposed change helps the manuscript.

alternativeGroup.description: Shared issue label linking alternative proposals; alternatives remain independent and revision guarded.

query.description: Inbox search across labels and rationale.

after.description: Inbox cursor from nextCursor; reset after changing filters.

idempotencyKey.description: Stable caller key to avoid creating duplicate proposals after a retry.

operationId.description: Application UUID to undo or to identify a retried application.

allowFormattingLoss.description: Explicitly acknowledge formatting risks disclosed by preview before applying.

force.description: Explicitly override native-app open/ambiguous detection only; never overrides revisions or server-instance conflicts.

result.description: Persistent proposal, before/after preview, guarded application, batch, recovery or undo result. List actions return proposals; recover returns applications.

tools.name: analyze_change_impact
tools.title: Preview Story Change Impact
tools.description: Preview a saved scene replacement, removal or move against cited story facts, continuity findings and author-recorded causal, timeline and revelation dependencies. Returns source evidence and candidate name references without modifying the manuscript; stale revisions fail.

documentId.description: Saved scene whose change is being evaluated.

expectedRevision.description: Current saved RTF revision; stale requests fail.

kind.description: Hypothetical change; never mutates the manuscript.

replacementText.description: Complete hypothetical scene text for replace, unless proposalId is supplied.

proposalId.description: Use an existing guarded review preview instead of replacementText.

beforeDocumentId.description: Move before this scene; null means the end of the manuscript.

terms.description: Additional names or terms to locate as candidate downstream references.

limit.description: Maximum returned impacts; total and truncated disclose omitted results.

result.description: Revision-bound advisory impact report or persistent dependency result.

tools.name: story_dependencies
tools.title: Record Story Dependencies
tools.description: Record author-confirmed causal, timeline or revelation dependencies between two verified saved scene passages, list them with bounded pagination, or remove an obsolete relationship. These annotations support advisory change-impact previews and never edit manuscript text.

action.description: List, record or remove an author-confirmed dependency.

id.description: Dependency identity to remove.

kind.description: Author-assigned relationship meaning.

projectId.description: Source project identity.

documentId.description: Source scene UUID.

revision.description: Saved source revision.

start.description: Inclusive UTF-16 offset.

end.description: Exclusive UTF-16 offset.

dependent.description: Verified passage depending on the prerequisite.

projectId.description: Source project identity.

documentId.description: Source scene UUID.

revision.description: Saved source revision.

start.description: Inclusive UTF-16 offset.

end.description: Exclusive UTF-16 offset.

explanation.description: Why this dependency matters to the story.

after.description: Next-page cursor from the prior list response.

result.description: Revision-bound advisory impact report or persistent dependency result.

tools.name: search
tools.title: Search Documents
tools.description: Search the open project and return matching documents with literal excerpts. By default performs literal full-text search across the active binder, including research and excluded drafts; set field to "title" for a fast case-insensitive title lookup, or scope to "trash" to search only trashed documents. For meaning-based "find passages about X" queries use semantic_search; to find every occurrence of a specific name or term use find_mentions. Requires an open project.

query.description: Search query: keywords for full-text search, or a natural-language phrase for semantic search, depending on the tool.

field.description: "content" (default) searches document body text; "title" matches document titles only (fast, case-insensitive substring).

scope.description: "active" (default) searches the live binder; "trash" searches only trashed documents.

caseSensitive.description: Match case exactly. Default false. Applies to content search.

regex.description: Treat the query as a regular expression. Default false. Content search only.

searchIn.description: Additional metadata fields to include in content search, e.g. "synopsis", "notes".

results.description: Matching documents. Field set varies by search mode: content/semantic searches return id/title/snippet/score; title search returns id/title/type/path; trash search returns documentId/title/matches.

id.description: Document id.

documentId.description: Document id (trash-scope results).

score.description: Relevance score, or null when unranked.

tools.name: list_trash
tools.title: List Trash
tools.description: List all documents currently in the project trash, with their ids and titles. Use this to see what can be brought back with restore_document, or to confirm a delete_document call. Requires an open project. Takes no parameters.

items.description: Documents currently in the project trash, in binder order.

id.description: Document id.

type.description: Binder item type (Text, Folder, or Other).

tools.name: restore_document
tools.title: Restore Document From Trash
tools.description: Restore a trashed document back into the binder, optionally into a specific target folder (otherwise it returns to a default location). Use list_trash to find the document id first. This is the inverse of delete_document. Requires an open project and a valid document id.

documentId.description: Scrivener document UUID, as returned by get_structure (a binder item "id").

targetFolderId.description: Optional id of the folder to restore into. Omit to restore to a default location.

force.description: Explicitly acknowledge native-app overwrite risk when Scrivener is open or detection is ambiguous. Default false. Never overrides saved revision checks or another server instance.

dryRun.description: Validate and preview the structural change without writing. Reuse the returned expectedRevision when applying.

expectedRevision.description: Binder revision returned by a structural preview. A changed binder rejects the operation.

tools.name: read_annotations
tools.title: Read Document Annotations
tools.description: Return the inline comments and footnotes attached to a document, grouped by type. Use this to review editorial notes and references without reading the full body; use read_document for the prose itself. Requires an open project and a valid document id.

documentId.description: Scrivener document UUID, as returned by get_structure (a binder item "id").

comments.description: Inline comments as [key, value] pairs, where key identifies the comment and value is its text.

footnotes.description: Footnotes as [key, value] pairs, where key identifies the footnote and value is its text.

tools.name: find_mentions
tools.title: Find Entity Mentions
tools.description: Find every occurrence of a specific name or term (a character, place, or keyword) across all documents, returning each hit with surrounding context and its document. Use this for exact "where does X appear" lookups; use search for relevance-ranked results or semantic_search for meaning-based matches. Returns up to 50 mentions. Requires an open project.

entity.description: The exact name or term to locate, e.g. a character name like "Elena".

contextLength.description: Number of characters of surrounding context to include on each side of a match. Default 100.

mentions.description: Occurrences of the entity, up to 50, each with surrounding context.

id.description: Id of the document containing the match.

snippet.description: Context around the match, truncated to 100 characters.

tools.name: semantic_search
tools.title: Semantic Search
tools.description: Find passages with configured local model embeddings or default story-concept vectors without an API key, and return the most relevant passages with similarity scores and surrounding text. Use this for conceptual "find passages about X" queries; use search for keyword/full-text matching and find_mentions to locate every occurrence of a specific name or term. Indexing and similarity scoring and optional reranking are local; each response discloses the configured model or bounded concept vocabulary. Requires an open project with semantic indexing available.

tools.name: analyze_manuscript_local
tools.title: Analyze Manuscript with Narrative Lens
tools.description: Analyze the saved manuscript locally with Narrative Lens: evidence-located findings, coverage, author intentions, chronology and revision comparisons. tools.name: check_style_local
tools.title: Check Style (Local)
tools.description: Line-edit one document with deterministic rules: -ly adverbs, filter words (felt, saw, noticed), hedges and intensifiers (just, really, very), stock clichés, passive voice, nominalizations, and any personal tics you name. Returns every finding with its line, column, and excerpt, plus counts and rates per 1,000 words so documents of different lengths compare. No AI model and no network call -- use enhance_content when you want the prose rewritten rather than flagged. Requires an open project and a valid document id.

documentId.description: Scrivener document UUID, as returned by get_structure (a binder item "id").

tics.description: Words or phrases you overuse (e.g. "suddenly", "a beat"). Flagged with rule "tic".

maxFindings.description: Cap on findings returned, in document order. Default 200.

counts.description: Findings per rule: adverbs, filterWords, hedges, cliches, tics, passive, nominalizations.

findings.description: Findings in document order: rule, message, location {line, column, offset, length, excerpt}, inDialogue.

tools.name: find_repetition_local
tools.title: Find Repetition (Local)
tools.description: Find echoes (the same word reappearing within a window of words) and repeated multi-word phrases in one document, each with line, column, and excerpt for both occurrences. Stopwords and, by default, capitalized names are ignored. No AI model and no network call. Requires an open project and a valid document id.

documentId.description: Scrivener document UUID, as returned by get_structure (a binder item "id").

window.description: Max words between two uses for them to count as an echo. Default 50.

minLength.description: Shortest word (in characters) to consider for echoes. Default 4.

includeNames.description: Count capitalized names as echoes too. Default false.

minPhraseWords.description: Shortest repeated phrase, in words. Default 3.

maxPhraseWords.description: Longest repeated phrase, in words. Default 6.

minPhraseCount.description: Fewest occurrences for a phrase to be reported. Default 2.

echoes.description: Echoes: word, distance (words apart), first and second locations.

repeats.description: Repeated phrases, most frequent first: phrase, words, count, locations.

tools.name: analyze_rhythm_local
tools.title: Analyze Rhythm (Local)
tools.description: Measure sentence-length flow in one document: the distribution of sentence lengths, a variation score (stdev over mean; low reads as monotonous), runs of same-length sentences, overlong sentences, and sentences or paragraphs that keep opening with the same word. Each finding carries a line and column. No AI model and no network call. Requires an open project and a valid document id.

documentId.description: Scrivener document UUID, as returned by get_structure (a binder item "id").

run.description: Consecutive similar-length sentences that count as monotonous. Default 4.

tolerance.description: Word-count difference still considered the same length. Default 3.

long.description: Sentence length in words flagged as overlong. Default 40.

starterRun.description: Consecutive sentences opening with the same word to flag. Default 3.

summary.description: Sentence-length distribution: count, mean, median, stdev, min, max.

variation.description: Stdev over mean of sentence length.

lengths.description: Word count of every sentence, in order.

findings.description: monotony, long-sentence, and repeated-starter findings with locations.

starters.description: Most common sentence and paragraph openers with counts.

tools.name: analyze_dialogue_tags_local
tools.title: Analyze Dialogue Tags (Local)
tools.description: Audit dialogue in one document: the dialogue-to-narration ratio and every quoted line with its attribution classified as plain (said, asked), showy (exclaimed, snapped), adverb-modified (said softly), or untagged, with the speaker when one can be read from the tag. No AI model and no network call -- complements analyze_craft_local, which extracts dialogue for speaker inference rather than tag quality. Requires an open project and a valid document id.

documentId.description: Scrivener document UUID, as returned by get_structure (a binder item "id").

maxAttributions.description: Cap on attributions returned, in document order. Default 200.

ratio.description: dialogueWords, narrationWords, and ratio (share of words in dialogue).

plainTags.description: Lines tagged with said/asked and inflections.

adverbTags.description: Lines whose tag carries an adverb.

untagged.description: Quoted lines with no attribution verb.

attributions.description: Each quoted line: dialogue location, tag location, kind (plain|showy|null), adverb, speaker.

tools.name: manuscript_style_report_local
tools.title: Manuscript Style Report (Local)
tools.description: Run the bluepencil report over every manuscript document in binder order and tabulate per-document style density: words, Flesch-Kincaid grade, dialogue ratio, lexical diversity (MATTR), mean sentence length, and adverbs, filter words, hedges, passive voice, and echoes per 1,000 words, plus clichés, monotonous runs, and overlong sentences. Outliers are listed so you can see which chapters drift from the rest. No AI model and no network call. Requires an open project.

includeExcluded.description: Include documents with "Include in Compile" off. Default false, matching the manuscript as it would actually compile.

tics.description: Words or phrases you overuse, counted as tics in each document.

documents.description: One row per document, in binder order, with the metrics above.

totals.description: Manuscript-wide words and word-weighted means of each rate.

outliers.description: Documents more than 1.5 standard deviations from the manuscript mean on a rate (needs at least four documents with text): documentId, title, metric, value, mean.

tools.name: set_writing_goal
tools.title: Set Writing Goal
tools.description: Create or replace the active word-count goal for a cadence (daily, weekly, or whole project), optionally with a target date. Setting a goal of a type that already has an active goal updates that goal in place rather than stacking duplicates. Use when the writer commits to a target ("write 1000 words a day", "finish an 80k novel by December"); not when you only want to read current progress (use get_writing_goals) or log a finished session. Related: get_writing_goals, predict_completion. Requires the project database.

type.description: Goal cadence: "daily" or "weekly" track words written in that window; "project" tracks the whole manuscript toward a final length.

targetWords.description: Target word count for this goal, a positive whole number (e.g. 1000 for a daily goal, 80000 for a novel-length project goal).

targetDate.description: Optional deadline as an ISO date, e.g. "2026-12-31". Used to judge whether progress is on pace. Omit for an open-ended goal.

tools.name: get_writing_goals
tools.title: Get Writing Goals
tools.description: List writing goals with computed progress: percent complete, words remaining, and whether each goal is on pace given its target date and the current project word count. Use when the writer asks how close they are to a goal or for a progress dashboard; not when defining a new goal (use set_writing_goal) or forecasting a finish date from writing velocity (use predict_completion). Related: set_writing_goal. Requires an open project and the project database.

status.description: Optional filter by goal status. Omit to list goals of every status; use "active" to see only goals still in progress.

goals.description: Goals with computed progress; empty when none match the filter.

id.description: Goal identifier.

targetWords.description: Target word count for the goal.

targetDate.description: ISO deadline, or null for an open-ended goal.

achievedWords.description: Words counted toward the goal (live project words for "project" goals, recorded words otherwise).

wordsRemaining.description: Words left to reach the target, never negative.

onTrack.description: Whether achieved words meet the pace implied by the target date.

projectWords.description: Current total word count of the open project.

tools.name: set_writing_preferences
tools.title: Set Writing Preferences
tools.description: Set the author writing preferences that shape AI writing output (enhance_content and other generative tools). Preferences are injected into the AI prompt, so changes take effect on the next enhancement. All fields are optional and merge into the existing profile. Use when the writer states a preferred tone, complexity, length, point of view, style guide, or a custom instruction. Requires an open project (preferences persist in the project database).

enabled.description: Master switch. When false, preferences are kept but not applied to AI output.

pointOfView.description: Narrative point of view to maintain, e.g. "third-person limited". Free text; pass an empty string to clear.

styleGuides.description: Style guides to honour, e.g. ["Chicago"]. Replaces the existing list; pass [] to clear.

customInstructions.description: Free-form instruction appended verbatim to the AI directive. Pass an empty string to clear.

tools.name: get_writing_preferences
tools.title: Get Writing Preferences
tools.description: Return the current author writing preferences plus feedback insights: how much feedback has been recorded, average satisfaction per operation, and non-binding suggestions for adjusting preferences. Use to review what is currently steering AI output, or to see whether recorded feedback points to a change. Related: set_writing_preferences, collect_feedback. Requires an open project.

enabled.description: When false, preferences are not applied to AI output.

pointOfView.description: Narrative point of view, when set.

customInstructions.description: Free-form instruction appended to the AI directive, when set.

updatedAt.description: ISO timestamp of the last preference update, when known.

insights.description: Aggregated feedback view plus non-binding suggestions.

overallAverageRating.description: Mean of all provided ratings, or null when none were rated.

operation.description: The operation the aggregate is for.

count.description: Number of feedback events for this operation.

averageRating.description: Mean rating for this operation, or null when none rated.

acceptanceRate.description: Fraction of events accepted, or null when none recorded acceptance.

suggestions.description: Human-readable, non-binding suggestions derived from feedback.

tools.name: collect_feedback
tools.title: Collect Feedback
tools.description: Record feedback on an AI operation (e.g. "enhance_content") so it feeds the insights returned by get_writing_preferences. Provide a 1-5 rating, whether the output was kept (accepted), and/or a comment. Use after the writer reacts to AI output. Requires an open project.

operation.description: The operation being rated, e.g. "enhance_content" or "compile_documents".

accepted.description: Whether the AI output was kept (true) or discarded (false). Optional.

tools.name: continuity_findings
tools.title: Review Evidence-Based Continuity Findings
tools.description: List persistent continuity findings with quoted source passages, confirm a concern, dismiss an intentional variation, resolve it, or rerun local analysis and recheck saved source revisions. Finding confirmation records the author review decision; it does not promote inferred narrative statements to confirmed story facts.

after.description: Cursor from nextCursor in a previous list result.

limit.description: List page size, default20; results use stable ID order.

action.description: Finding review or source revision recheck operation.

findingId.description: Required for confirm, dismiss or resolve; optional for rechecking one finding.

note.description: Author decision note, at most 2000 characters.

includeResolved.description: Include dismissed and resolved findings when listing.

nextCursor.description: Next finding cursor, or null after the final list page.

findings.description: Findings in binder order with evidence and review state.

id.description: Persistent finding identity tied to the source revisions.

documentId.description: Primary document identity in the open manuscript.

tools.name: compile_documents
tools.title: Compile Documents
tools.description: Compile the project's documents into a single continuous manuscript in the requested format and return the compiled text (large results include a resultId for read_result). In "standard" mode it joins documents in binder order; in "intelligent" mode it uses AI to optimize the output for a specific target such as an agent query or synopsis. AI rewrites require the complete source to fit 12000 UTF-16 characters; otherwise the complete original is preserved with warnings. Provider quality assessments cover at most 4000 characters and declare unavailable fields. Intelligent results include saved revisions and reject source changes during generation. To write a manuscript to disk in a publishing format (EPUB, etc.) use export_project instead. Requires an open project.

mode.description: "standard" (default) joins documents in order; "structured" compiles the Draft/Manuscript folder (like Scrivener) with the binder hierarchy as headings and a scene separator between documents, honoring each document's "Include in Compile" flag — deterministic, no AI; "intelligent" applies AI optimization toward targetOptimization.

format.description: Output format of the compiled manuscript. Default "text".

rootFolderId.description: Optional binder folder id to compile only its descendants. Omit to compile all text documents.

documentIds.description: Optional explicit list of document ids to compile, in order. Overrides rootFolderId when provided; most useful with mode "intelligent".

targetOptimization.description: For mode "intelligent": what to optimize the compiled output for. Default "general".

includeSynopsis.description: Include each document's synopsis in the output. Default false.

includeNotes.description: Include each document's notes in the output. Default false.

Text inserted between documents in the standard-mode fallback. Default "

".

includeTitles.description: For mode "structured": emit each document title as a heading. Default true.

includeExcluded.description: For mode "structured": include documents whose "Include in Compile" flag is off. Default false (excluded documents are omitted, matching Scrivener).

compileFormatId.description: For mode "structured": id of a compile format from get_compile_settings. When given, sections whose resolved Section Type maps to one of that format's recognized standard layouts (title visibility, chapter auto-numbering, page breaks) use that layout's behavior instead of includeTitles/sceneSeparator. Custom or unrecognized layouts fall back to the generic behavior — this is best-effort, not full Scrivener compile fidelity.

tools.name: export_project

tools.name: queue_document_analysis
tools.title: Queue Document Analysis
tools.description: Enqueue local analysis of supplied text with a SHA-256 source revision and raw policy. Base prose analysis always runs; readability is included by default. Optional named entities require a local Narrative Lens NER model; sentiment uses a local lexicon heuristic. Unavailable sections are explicit. return a job id immediately without blocking. Poll the job with get_job_status and request cancellation with cancel_job. Use this for large documents where a synchronous analyze_document call would be slow; use analyze_document directly for quick, inline results.

documentId.description: Scrivener document UUID, as returned by get_structure (a binder item "id").

options.description: Optional result sections and scheduling priority; base prose analysis always runs.

includeEntities.description: Include native named-entity extraction or an explicit unavailable result when the native build or model is unavailable. Default false.

includeSentiment.description: Include local lexicon sentiment scores; these are heuristic signals, not model probabilities. Default false.

priority.description: Default 0 runs before prioritized jobs; lower positive numbers run sooner. Nonzero priorities require Redis or KeyDB.

jobId.description: Identifier of the queued job; poll it with get_job_status.

tools.description: Enqueue local analysis of 1–5000 supplied document texts, preserving input order and a source revision per document, and return a job id immediately. Poll progress with get_job_status and request cancellation with cancel_job. Use this to analyze a whole manuscript or large set of documents; for a single document prefer queue_document_analysis or the synchronous analyze_document.

tools.name: suggest_improvements
tools.title: Suggest Improvements
tools.description: Generate AI writing suggestions for a prompt or a specific document — ideas for revision, next steps, or alternatives. Returns suggestion text, context coverage and a provenance envelope; large results use read_result references. With useContext, sends up to the first 16000 UTF-16 characters of the saved document to the configured provider, checking its revision before and after generation. Queued jobs return the same result through get_job_status and are not automatically retried. Use this for generative "how could this be better" help; use analyze_document for structured metrics or check_consistency to find contradictions.
